question: A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above their cost price. He sells 60% of the goods at the marked price and the remaining at 65% discount on the marked price. His gain/loss in the whole transaction is:
solution:
**Given:**

Shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above CP

He sells 60% of the goods at MP and remaining at 65% discount on MP

**Formula used:**

Profit = (SP-CP)/(CP) × 100

**Calculation:**

Let CP be ₹100

Let the total number of goods be 100

Total CP = 100 × 100 = ₹10000

According to the question,

MP = 100 × (140/100) = ₹140

Total SP = [100×(60)/(100)×140] + [100×(40)/(100)×140×(35)/(100)]

⇒ Total SP = 8400 + 1960 = ₹10360

Profit% = (10360-10000)/(10000) × 100 = 3.6%

**∴ The shopkeeper gains 3.6% profit in the whole transaction.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**MP = ₹140 and SP (at 65% discount) = ₹49

Ratio of goods sold at MP to sold at 65% is 60:40 = 3:2

Here, 140 - 49 = 91, thus 91/(3+2) = 18.2
